solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Daredevil sister's clothing used to be hard to fold

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap round it, so the sister's letters go on the outside of the rest

parts.note: Sr is the standard abbreviation for Sister, as in a nun or senior nurse
used to be means was, the past tense
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
to fold under pressure is to buckle

explanation.surface: A nun's old habit was so stiff that it would not fold, a daredevil garment indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive on 'sister's' carries the containment: her clothing is what goes around everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashing, swaggering adventurer of the pirate-film type is a reckless daredevil.

clue.text: At least three opuses identifying northern town

parts.note: works is a plural, so two or more opuses
op is the abbreviation for opus, one more, making at least three in all

explanation.surface: A musicologist identifies a northern town from a handful of compositions written there.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural WORKS means at least two opuses; adding one more OP gives at least three. Worksop is a town in north Nottinghamshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Worksop is a market town in Nottinghamshire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Carts overturned carrying fruit for Harland & Wolff?

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the fruit goes within the carts
in a down clue overturned means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: drays are low heavy carts, as used by brewers
a hip is the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: Carts tip over spilling fruit at the Belfast works of Harland & Wolff.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAYS read upwards is SYARD, which takes in HIP. Harland & Wolff is the Belfast firm that built the Titanic, hence the question mark for a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Harland & Wolff is a famous shipbuilding firm, an example of a yard where vessels are constructed.

clue.text: Save end of ticket stub

parts.note: save in the sense of except means but

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word ticket

explanation.surface: Keep the torn-off end of your ticket as proof of entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like a verb but means except.
explanation.definitionFit: The stub of a cigarette or a ticket is its leftover end, also called a butt.

clue.text: China's triumph — new revolutionary Communist times

parts.note: to crow is to triumph or exult boastfully

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: red is a common word for a Communist
by means times, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A headline on China's victory in a new era of revolutionary Communism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' with a capital looks like the country but means porcelain; 'revolutionary' turns the Communist colour, giving DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Crown Derby is a famous English make of porcelain, and fine porcelain is called china.

clue.text: Fail to get round in — that's lax

indicators.note: in places the round shape within the word for failing to get

parts.note: to fail to get something is to lose it
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A slack golfer cannot get round the course in par, which is lax.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose and lax are synonyms for slack or not strict.

clue.text: Dictator abandoning first desperate measure to keep order

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild and frantic, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new arrangement
abandoning first means dropping the opening letter of the word dictator

explanation.surface: A dictator gives up his first desperate measure for keeping public order.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing D from DICTATOR leaves ICTATOR, which 'desperate' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading the Riot Act was the formal warning to disperse a crowd, a step to restore public order.

clue.text: One has brief stay in hospital? It may be packed

definitions.text: One has brief stay in hospital?
definitions.meaning: a patient kept on the ward for just one night would be such a case in medical terms
a small bag holding enough clothes for one night away is packed before a trip

explanation.surface: A patient on a short hospital visit packs a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading treats 'case' as a medical patient admitted for a single night.
explanation.definitionFit: A small suitcase for a one-night trip, and punningly a patient kept in hospital for a single night.

clue.text: This writer has confidence in white-haired minister

indicators.note: in places the writer and the confidence within the word for white-haired

parts.note: hoary means grey or white with age
the setter refers to themself as this writer, giving me
a confidence is something told in secret, a secret

explanation.surface: The author confides in a grey-haired government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Secretary is the UK government minister in charge of policing and immigration.
explanation.definitionFit: The Home Secretary is the senior British cabinet minister responsible for internal affairs.

clue.text: Short change given by perfect rascal

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the final letter of the word for change is lost

parts.note: to vary is to change
mint, as in mint condition, means perfect

explanation.surface: A scoundrel short-changes customers while handing over perfect-looking coins.
explanation.walkthrough: VARY loses its last letter to give VAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A varmint is a dialect word for a troublesome person or animal, a rascal.

clue.text: Sadly, daughter lost the sherry

indicators.note: lost means the daughter is taken away from the musical term

parts.note: doloroso is the musical direction meaning sadly or plaintively

explanation.surface: Sadly, a daughter has gone and lost the bottle of sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' looks like an anagram signal but is the musical term DOLOROSO; dropping D leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oloroso is a rich, dark style of Spanish sherry from Jerez.

clue.text: Run independent broadcaster? That's uncertain

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster

explanation.surface: Is running an independent television channel a gamble with an uncertain outcome?
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: Something risky is hazardous, its outcome far from sure.

clue.text: Eg R. Benaud bowled out bats for less than 18?

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the letters are scrambled
out means the bowled letter is removed from the cricketer's name

parts.note: Richie Benaud, the Australian cricket captain and commentator
B is the scorecard abbreviation for bowled in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: Richie Benaud bowls out a batsman who is not yet eighteen.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking B from RBENAUD leaves RENAUD; with EG, 'bats' rearranges the lot. Richie Benaud was a famous Australian cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being younger than eighteen means being below the legal adult age in Britain.

clue.text: Religious art needs to change still, so they say

indicators.note: so they say signals the words are heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: to change is to alter, and still means peace or quiet

explanation.surface: Religious art must change, though it is still, according to some.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting or carving set behind a church altar is a classic piece of religious artwork.

clue.text: Small state captured by force was first to be threatened

indicators.note: captured by means held inside the word for force

parts.note: to impel is to force or drive
RI is Rhode Island, the smallest US state
to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: A small country was seized by force and became the first to be under threat.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhode Island (RI) is the smallest US state.
explanation.definitionFit: To be imperilled is to be put in danger, that is under threat.

clue.text: In honesty, enthusiasm is swelling

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: Honest enthusiasm is growing, the clue says, with a hint of pomp.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small inflamed swelling on the eyelid.

clue.text: She needs Orange mobile to ring soldier

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the scrambled letters go round the soldier
mobile means able to move, so the letters of orange shift about

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A woman needs her Orange mobile phone to call a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Orange was a British mobile phone network, so 'mobile' reads as a phone; here it reorders the brand name into GEORNA.
explanation.definitionFit: She stands for any female, and the answer is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Dance heralding athletic Kiwi appearances, for starters?

indicators.note: for starters means taking only the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A dance announces the first appearances of New Zealand athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Zealand rugby team perform this dance before matches, so the clue nearly reads as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The haka is a Maori ceremonial war dance, famously performed by the All Blacks.

clue.text: Congenial sort appearing ashamed?

parts.note: a sort is a kind, as in type
someone ashamed goes red in the face

explanation.surface: A pleasant type of person who looks embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congenial sort' reads as one person, but 'sort' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred, as in kindred spirits, describes people of like mind who get on well.

clue.text: Judge wants criminal beheaded? It's hard to say

indicators.note: beheaded means losing the first letter

parts.note: a lawbreaker is a criminal

explanation.surface: A judge wants a criminal beheaded, though that is hard to say aloud in court.
explanation.walkthrough: LAWBREAKER loses its L.
explanation.definitionFit: A long tongue-twisting word that is difficult to pronounce is jokingly called by this name.

clue.text: In part of Hull on vacation, spot river bird

indicators.note: in means the following letters sit within the part of the hull

parts.note: the keel is the bottom part of a ship's hull

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, so only the outside letters remain

explanation.surface: On holiday near the city of Hull, someone spots a river bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hull' looks like the English city but is a ship's hull; 'on vacation' empties 'spot' to its outer letters ST.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is a small falcon that hovers over fields.

clue.text: One who's right to attract disdain

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, one on the political right
to tempt is to attract or lure

explanation.surface: Someone always in the right only attracts scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' means right-wing, not correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt and disdain both mean scorn for something thought worthless.

clue.text: Leaves to be with son at the end

indicators.note: at the end says the son's letter is moved to the final position

parts.note: to exist is to be

explanation.surface: A father leaves his estate to his son at the end of his life.
explanation.definitionFit: Exits as a verb means goes out, the same as leaves.

clue.text: Withdrawn weapon was tested again

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a Taser is a stun-gun weapon

explanation.surface: A police weapon is withdrawn after being tested again.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who resat an exam sat it a second time, being examined again.

clue.text: Biblical character of news- value, periodically

indicators.note: periodically picks every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A Bible figure has some news value now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau is Jacob's twin brother in Genesis, who sold his birthright.

clue.text: Obsequious performance of duty gets pound for Charlie

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: service is the performance of a duty
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A grovelling servant is paid a pound for his duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' joins: SERVICE gets L in place of C.
explanation.definitionFit: Servile and obsequious both describe fawning, excessive eagerness to please.

clue.text: Troublemaker mischievously tries to secure rights

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the scrambled letters wrap round the rights
mischievously suggests the letters are played about with

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right, so two rights give RR

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker tries to get hold of rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tries' looks like the verb of the surface but is the anagram fodder, which 'mischievously' turns into STIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrer is someone who stirs up trouble between others, a mischief-maker.

clue.text: Dodgy hamstring conceals pure sporting talent at first

indicators.note: conceals means holding the following letters hidden inside

parts.note: to hamstring is to cripple or disable

indicators.note: sporting suggests playing about, so the letters are rearranged
at first takes the opening letter of talent

explanation.surface: A hamstring injury hides an athlete's pure sporting talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' looks like it describes the hamstring but is the definition; 'sporting' reorders the pure letters as REPU.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgy in British slang means shady or untrustworthy, of poor repute.
